slides.title: 6 developments change the picture, led by Pulse, Northstar and Harbour
slides.measure: Developments that pass significance and materiality tests · level and change

rows.label: Pulse · Unaided awareness
rows.text: Pulse unaided awareness rose 14 pts to 45% in W3, with preference share (+7 pts) and customer share (+5 pts) moving the same way; W5 is still 13 pts above W2

rows.label: Northstar · Satisfaction (mean, 0–10)
rows.text: Northstar average satisfaction fell 1.5 points to 6.2 out of 10 in W4, with NPS (−48 pts) and share reporting a network problem (+20 pts) moving the same way; W5 is still 0.5 points below W3

rows.label: Harbour · Most preferred
rows.text: Harbour preference share has fallen gradually, −4.4 pts from W1 to W5, with no single wave-on-wave step significant

rows.label: Lumen · Most preferred
rows.text: Lumen preference share fell 4 pts to 7% in W3; W5 is still 3 pts below W2

rows.label: Northstar · Most preferred
rows.text: Northstar preference share has fallen gradually, −5.3 pts from W1 to W5, with no single wave-on-wave step significant

slides.source: Base: all respondents, n≈2,000 per wave (W1, W2, W3, W4, W5). Weighted (wt_final). Significance: Wald test on Kish effective bases, 95%, wave on wave unless stated. Materiality: ±3 pts for percentages, ±10 for NPS.

slides.title: Northstar leads every stage of the funnel in W5
slides.measure: Brand funnel, W5 · % of all respondents
slides.source: Base: all respondents in W5, n=2,000. Weighted. Consideration counts non-aware respondents as not considering.

slides.title: Pulse unaided awareness rose 14 pts to 45% in W3; W5 is still 13 pts above W2
slides.source: Base: All respondents. Unweighted base, Pulse: W1 2000, W2 2000, W3 2000, W4 2000, W5 2000. Weighted. Significance: Wald test on Kish effective bases, 95%, wave on wave unless stated.

slides.title: Northstar average satisfaction fell 1.5 points to 6.2 out of 10 in W4; W5 is still 0.5 points below W3
slides.measure: Satisfaction (mean, 0–10) · mean score · current customers of the brand
slides.source: Base: Current customers of the brand. Unweighted base, Northstar: W1 658, W2 660, W3 622, W4 612, W5 640. Weighted. Significance: Wald test on Kish effective bases, 95%, wave on wave unless stated.

slides.title: Harbour preference share has fallen gradually, −4.4 pts from W1 to W5, with no single wave-on-wave step significant
slides.source: Base: All respondents. Unweighted base, Harbour: W1 2000, W2 2000, W3 2000, W4 2000, W5 2000. Weighted. Significance: Wald test on Kish effective bases, 95%, wave on wave unless stated.

slides.title: Lumen preference share fell 4 pts to 7% in W3; W5 is still 3 pts below W2
slides.source: Base: All respondents. Unweighted base, Lumen: W1 2000, W2 2000, W3 2000, W4 2000, W5 2000. Weighted. Significance: Wald test on Kish effective bases, 95%, wave on wave unless stated.

slides.title: The W3 fall in Lumen preference share came from 18–34s (−6.3 pts) and 35–54s (−4.5 pts); those aged 55+ showed no significant change
slides.measure: Lumen preference share by age · W2 and W3
slides.source: Base: All respondents in each age group. Weighted. ▲/▼ change significant at 95%. Difference in change between 18–34 and 55+: p=0.014.

slides.title: Northstar preference share has fallen gradually, −5.3 pts from W1 to W5, with no single wave-on-wave step significant
slides.source: Base: All respondents. Unweighted base, Northstar: W1 2000, W2 2000, W3 2000, W4 2000, W5 2000. Weighted. Significance: Wald test on Kish effective bases, 95%, wave on wave unless stated.

slides.title: Among 18–34s, Harbour consideration among those aware has fallen 9.1 pts since W1; the total-market change is not significant
slides.measure: Consideration among aware · % · aware of the brand
slides.source: Base: Aware of the brand. Unweighted base, 18–34: W1 458, W2 426, W3 676, W4 425, W5 433. Weighted. Significance: Wald test on Kish effective bases, 95%, wave on wave unless stated.

slides.title: About this study
items: UK adults who decide or share the decision on their personal mobile service
Wave 1, Wave 2, Wave 3, Wave 4, Wave 5; 2,000 respondents per wave, fresh samples.
wt_final within each wave. Percentages are weighted; bases shown are unweighted.
Wald tests on Kish effective bases at 95%. Subgroup trends are screened at 99% because many are examined. Changes also need to exceed a materiality threshold before they are reported.
Routed questions use their own base (for example, image among those familiar with the brand; NPS among current customers). Bases under 50 are not used for claims.
slides.source: Synthetic five-wave tracker (SBT-001); brands and figures are fictitious.
